body:
DISCUSS BEFORE STARTING — no approach chosen yet.

server/src/shoppinglist_server/apk/shoppinglist.apk is committed on every
release and nothing ever leaves history. Measured today:

  .git                      52 MB
  19 committed APK blobs    ~45 MB of it
  per release               ~2.4 MB, growing with the app

The APK is a committed input on purpose — build-wheel.sh does not rebuild it,
and a fresh clone can build a complete wheel with no Android toolchain. That
property is worth keeping; the question is only how the bytes are stored.

Forward-only options (history is not to be rewritten):

1. git LFS from the next release on. Keeps the checkout property, moves new
   blobs out of the pack. Adds an LFS dependency for anyone cloning.
2. Stop tracking the APK; release.sh copies it from the Android build output
   and it ships as a release asset instead. Smallest repo, but a clone can no
   longer build the full wheel without the Android toolchain.
3. Accept it. ~2.4 MB per release is not a real problem yet at this rate.

Note option 2 conflicts with the single-deployable-artifact story in the README
as currently written, so picking it means rewriting that section too.
title: Embedded APK blobs grow the repo ~2.4 MB per release — decide a policy
